title: Token Cohort Explorer + Failover Rehearsal Dashboard: instrument golden signals and SLI cohorts
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary:
We need a cohesive instrumentation and dashboarding initiative that surfaces token-level latency SLIs across cohorts (token length, prefix cache hit, model-variant, priority path, region) and couples those cohorts to a 'failover rehearsal' panel that simulates multi-region degradation and shows circuit-breaker state, admission rates, and projected SLO burn. The goal is to make root-cause and mitigation decisions faster during region partial failures and to validate load-shedding policies using synthetic rehearsals before a real event.

Why this work:
- Current token SLI dashboards are noisy at the aggregate level; regressions are often localized to specific cohorts (long-context requests, cold KV caches, or model-variant fallbacks).
- Runbooks for regional failover are manual; we need a rehearsal surface that ties metrics to policy outcomes (who gets shed, which model fallbacks activate, and expected SLO burn).
- We want a reproducible harness to validate new admission heuristics and hysteresis settings without risking customer traffic.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
1) Instrumentation: ingest token-level golden signals for cohorts: token_latency_ms_bucketed, token_decode_time_ms, token_admit_score, kv_cache_hit, region, model_variant, priority_path, sequence_length_bucket. Retention: 30d for full histogram aggregates, 90d for downsampled rollups.
2) Cohort Explorer UI: dashboard with interactive cohort selector, showing p50/p95/p99 token latency, admission rate, kv-hit rate, and failover impact projection for the selected cohort.
3) Rehearsal Panel: a playbook-driven simulator that replays synthetic traffic into a copy of the routing/policy logic and visualizes which circuits open, how traffic is rerouted across regions, and the resulting SLO projections.
4) Low overhead: sampling rate defaults to 1% for full-token traces, configurable up to 10% for PD testing; all instrumentation must add <1% CPU overhead on the serving process at default sampling.
5) Alerts: create derived SLI alerts that trigger when cohort p99 exceeds SLO by 20% for 5m or when admission rate drops by >30% for a cohort.
6) Documentation & Runbook: link from dashboard to a one-page rehearshal runbook and remediation checklist in Confluence.

Implementation notes / trade-offs:
- Cohorting keys: we decided to keep cohort keys shallow (sequence_length_bucket, token_position_quartile, kv_cache_hit boolean, model_variant, region, priority_path) to limit cardinality. Using full-prefix hashing would explode storage and complicate realtime rollups.
- Storage vs fidelity: histogram buckets will be 10ms up to 2s, then coarse buckets. We will store high-fidelity histograms for sampled traces and rely on continuous quantile estimators for full traffic. This balances cost vs debug usefulness.
- Sampling: default low sampling for production; higher sampling will be used in dedicated/regression environments. We will provide a dynamic sampling API in the agent to raise sampling for specific customer IDs during on-call investigation.
- Rehearsal fidelity: simulation will not spin up real cross-region traffic but will replay decision logic with recorded admission scores and synthetic region latencies; we accept some realism loss for safety and repeatability.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Instrumentation (Week 1): add token-level emitters for the cohort keys and histogram buckets in the serving runtime. Use existing telemetry queue and add a new aggregator for cohort histograms. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/542 (WIP).
2) Backfill job (Week 1–2): backfill recent 7d into the new cohort aggregates for baseline comparisons. Job: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pull/98
3) Dashboard (Week 2): build Grafana dashboard panels and a Cohort Explorer plugin that lets you pivot cohorts and see the rehearshal projection. Dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/8X7Cohort/token-cohort-explorer (internal).
4) Rehearsal harness (Week 2–3): lightweight simulator service that consumes cohort aggregates and runs the routing/policy codepath in sandbox mode to output circuit states and SLO projection. Service PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rehearsal/pull/11
5) Alerts & Runbook (Week 3): add Alerts in Opsgenie and a Confluence page for the rehearsal playbook.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for histogram rollup and sampling correctness.
- End-to-end test using synthetic traffic in staging to ensure dashboard metrics match expected numbers.
- A small production canary: enable 2% extra sampling for a low-traffic shard for 48h and validate overhead metrics.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Retention and downsample windows: finance wants 7d high-fidelity only; reliability wants 30d. Proposal: 30d for histogram aggregates at cohort-level, 90d for quantile rollups only.
- Admission delta API: should raising sampling during incident require SRE approval? Proposed: allow SRE/SE to toggle via Console for short windows with audit logs.

Links & artifacts:
- Telemetry PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/542
- Rehearsal service: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rehearsal/pull/11
- Dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/8X7Cohort/token-cohort-explorer
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELIABILITY/Token+Cohort+Rehearsal+Runbook

Rollout plan:
- Alpha: staging dashboard + rehearsal runs with synthetic traffic; 2 engineers verify metric parity.
- Beta: enable sampled production telemetry for 2 shards; run 1 rehearsal and validate failover projection with oncall.
- GA: enable cohort rollups globally at default sampling and onboard SRE/SE training.
acceptance_criteria: Token-level cohort histograms are emitted and visible in Grafana for selected cohorts
Cohort Explorer can filter by region, model_variant, kv_cache_hit, and sequence_length_bucket
Rehearsal panel can run a simulated multi-region failover and show circuit states + SLO projection
Production overhead measured <1% CPU at default sampling (1%)
Alerts for cohort p99 breach and admission rate drops are created and tested
Runbook and one-pager published and linked from the dashboard
